Svelte expects the elements it renders to stay as it made them. When code removes, moves or rewrites one through the variable that `bind:this` sets, the DOM and Svelte's idea of it differ, and later updates break. The rule reports `remove()`, `append()`, `replaceWith()` and the other methods that change the tree, and assignments to `textContent`, `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `innerText` and `outerText`, on elements of HTML and `<svelte:element>`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-dom-manipulating": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  let banner;
  const dismiss = () => banner.remove();
</script>

<div bind:this={banner}>Saved</div>
<button on:click={dismiss}>Dismiss</button>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  let visible = true;
  const dismiss = () => (visible = false);
</script>

{#if visible}<div>Saved</div>{/if}
<button on:click={dismiss}>Dismiss</button>
```
